why_this_file_exists: The Phase 4 boundary is where R-17's committed baselines are re-captured. The pair baseline is clean and could move today; the coupled baseline may not, because R-19 forbids a re-capture while any qualifying occurrence lacks an oracle receipt and 60 of them do. That is not a defect in the tree: every one of the 145 differing coupled leaves is claimed by a committed allowlist, and the two S7 allowlists that own 59 of the 60 say so themselves (expected-golden-diff-P4-S7-bloodsong.json's oracle_receipts.status is 'OWED, NOT FILED'; expected-golden-diff-P4-S7-rearm.json's oracle_pass.status is 'OWED'). What has no artifact until this file is the boundary's own population: the S6/S7 oracle pass filed 82 receipts against the values the tree held on 2026-08-13, and the S7 rearm correction, the H5 stage and S9 moved 23 of those leaves again afterwards, so a receipt existing on a leaf path is no longer evidence that the value a re-capture would pin was ever adjudicated. Written down as a dated, gated artifact rather than as commit-body prose, because prose is exactly what the next baseline re-capture absorbs (R-16).
how_an_entry_closes: An entry moves from defects[] to retired[] only together with its gate test's own inversion: the reproducer stops reproducing and the test asserts the resolved property instead. For the entry below that means every leaf in owed_population carries a receipt whose certified new_value is the value the re-captured baseline holds, at which point the gate's no-covering-receipt assertion goes red and the entry retires carrying the population it named. Deleting an entry is not closing it. A retirement is not a release: the entry below retired on the day its receipts were filed, and the property it was protecting -- the committed coupled baseline still holding its old values -- is asserted by the same gate on behalf of its successor.

defects.raised_by: The R-18/R-19 investigator pass over the Phase 4 boundary's owed population, docs/receipts/oracle-P4B-leaf0.json through leaf59.json. 47 verdicts are new_value_correct; the 13 enumerated below are old_value_correct; none is both_wrong.
defects.what: R-19's verdict set makes old_value_correct a stop: a leaf whose independent verdict certifies the OLD value may not be pinned by a re-capture. 13 of the 60 boundary leaves carry that verdict, so scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json and scripts/golden_coupled_exact.json may not be re-captured, and the golden blocks of docs/receipts/campaign-fingerprints.json may not be refreshed, while this entry stands. The pair jurisdiction is unaffected and owes nothing (D-93).
defects.why_it_matters: The re-capture is the moment a diff becomes the campaign's authority. Absorbing 13 dissents into it would make the baseline assert 13 numbers an independent oracle said were wrong -- the campaign's own failure shape, an unexplained value wearing a gate's authority -- and it would do so irreversibly, because every later slice's diffs are read against whatever the baseline says.
defects.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: Every one of the 13 bears on a landed, separately ruled correction, not on anything this lane wrote. Eleven of them fall inside expected-golden-diff-P4-S7-rearm.json's declared population -- the S7 rearm correction ruled by D-13/D-62/D-66/D-92, itself raised by an oracle's both_wrong verdict (docs/receipts/oracle-S6S7-leaf46.json) and pinned by tests/test_modifier_rearm.py. Reverting it from a receipt-only commit would re-open a ruled decision and re-arm the defect it fixed; an implementation lane may do neither. The remaining two describe a heal whose amount did not move at all. So the disposition is escalation: the receipts are filed and committed, the verdicts are recorded verbatim, and the baselines stay exactly where they are.

the_third_owner_decision_is_now_ruled.amendment: docs/plans/silent-failure-runbook.md, section `Independent investigation`: **Amendment R-15/R-18 - 2026-08-14, briefing a leaf that cannot be judged alone.**
the_third_owner_decision_is_now_ruled.answers: for_the_owner item (3). R-18's investigator EXPORT does not move: it stays exactly data/ and docs/math-foundations.md, built by R-18's one git archive command. What moves is the BRIEF. For a leaf that is one member of a repeated-source series -- successive rows of a same-source list, successive arms of one debuff, or the fields of a record whose siblings did not move -- the brief additionally carries the question specification: the committed scenario parameters and the leaf's series position and context (timestamp, ordinal, trigger context, and the unmoved sibling facts), drawn ONLY from the committed PRE-change baseline receipt and the committed scenario definitions. Those are facts of the question and never facts of the fix, which is why the export rule needs no widening: the pre-change side is what the investigator is asked to adjudicate against, and a post-change sibling stays forbidden. Given that brief the investigator computes the ENTIRE series from scratch and issues one verdict per leaf.
the_third_owner_decision_is_now_ruled.and_rules_how_a_dissent_clears: Recorded beside it in the same amendment: a mechanic-level dissent cluster is re-adjudicated as ONE well-posed whole-series investigation by a fresh investigator that has read neither the prior receipts nor this escalation; a SUSTAINED dissent re-opens the producing correction as a ruled src/ fix with its own R-20 line and is never absorbed into a baseline; and a verdict is NEVER re-run merely because it dissents -- every re-run must cite the specific defect in the prior brief, written into the receipt that supersedes the prior one, which is never edited and never deleted. That last clause is the anti-oracle-shopping rule, and it is also this entry's licence: the defect its re-run would cite is the underdetermined question the amendment names, not the fact that thirteen verdicts disagreed.
the_third_owner_decision_is_now_ruled.why_this_entry_stays_open: The amendment rules the protocol, not the arithmetic. The arithmetic came back on 2026-08-14 and is recorded in re_adjudicated_under_the_amendment: eleven of the thirteen dissents are resolved by a whole-series pass and two are sustained, so scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json, scripts/golden_coupled_exact.json and the golden blocks of docs/receipts/campaign-fingerprints.json stand exactly where they were. Per how_an_entry_closes an entry retires only together with its gate test's own inversion; a protocol ruling is not that inversion, a partly-resolved enumeration is not either, and a sustained dissent is the one thing a re-capture may never absorb.

how_a_dissent_is_contradicted.contradicted_by: Receipts from this same pass that certify the contrary on the leaf the dissent turns on -- the surviving support_resistance_reduction[0] row, an adjacent removal in the same list, or another member of the same damage triple. Every name here carries the verdict new_value_correct.
how_a_dissent_is_contradicted.mutually_exclusive_with: Two dissents whose premises cannot both hold. oracle-P4B-leaf18 concludes healing_events[39]'s heal grew by a factor of 1.686 and oracle-P4B-leaf29 concludes the same heal fell by 22.3%; the record's `amount` is 359.4 in both trees, so neither premise holds and they refute each other before the baseline refutes them both. The relation is symmetric and the gate asserts it.
how_a_dissent_is_contradicted.why_a_row_may_carry_only_one: A dissent needs a stated contradiction, not a particular kind of one. Requiring a contrary sibling everywhere would have forced a false one onto the healing pair, which no receipt in the pass actually provides.
